content.comment_body: Split from another thread about hours counter issues.
This isn't a bug, just inconvenient. The slower data transfer is because communication uses HTTPS instead of HTTP.

I'm not convinced. Accessing a custom web page uses HTTP, not HTTPS, and browsers show whether a page is encrypted. The behavior differs between hardware and software versions; newer hardware is much slower. Firmware updates have helped before, but with the latest, loading is still slow. Fixing bugs could improve speed overall, but improvements can't happen as long as [company_name] prioritizes features like cloud connection.
I don't want to debate this. For me, it's only an issue if something is broken or only partially working.
Unlike older modules, the latest hardware now uses secure communication, which is why it's slower. Calculations themselves haven't changed.

I've tested both older and newer versions of the web editor. The newest is much slower on both hardware types, transferring data at only 20-50 KB/s, even for small amounts. Loading takes about ten minutes. It appears that reading and writing to the microSD card is slower with new editor versions, while CPU calculation speed seems unchanged. Once images and components are cached by the browser, loading is faster on subsequent attempts. If [company_name] can improve the web editor's interaction with the SD card, it would appeal more to users.

Usually, secure connections only use up to 10% more resources, not three to five times more. A German-speaking forum noted that encryption is required due to new regulations, possibly EU export restrictions. But there hasn't been an official statement demanding encrypted connections between all devices. On other company platforms, users can select communication security modes; it would be good to have similar choices in the web editor. Currently, warnings appear when activating unsecured ports, leaving it to user responsibility. The explanation for forced encryption feels more like a justification for not changing the current setup.

I've tested the same hardware version 8.3 with different web editor versions: 1.0 loads pages very quickly in non-secure mode, while 1.1 is 50-200% slower, even without secure mode. The speed is extremely slow in secure mode despite browser certificates. Even in non-secure mode, the newer editor version is always slower.
Web editor version 1.0.1 can't upload projects to the 8.3 hardware due to a firmware error.

I tested on 8.2 hardware (article_no hidden). The newer web editor version 1.1 uploads to 8.2 hardware but still causes slow loading. The problem seems to be with the software-created web pages, not the hardware itself. Using version 1.0 on both hardware types results in faster loading.

It's not possible to upload web editor 1.0 projects directly to 8.3 hardware, except possibly through SD card deployment. Project loading speed from a different editor (like [product_name]) is much faster, but with 8.3 hardware it's noticeably slower. Web editor projects are especially slow with latest hardware.

I confirm you can't upload web editor 1.0 projects directly to 8.3 hardware, only possibly via SD card. Also, the [product_name] project loading speed is different too (those projects were always very fast), but on 8.3 hardware they're noticeably slower. Web editor projects are extremely slow on 8.3. You need web editor 1.1 for 8.3, but it can also be used with 8.2. Web editor 1.1 makes all hardware slow and upload/download speeds poor, whereas using version 1.0 on both types solves the problem, though with fewer text and trend features.

Is there any workaround besides using 8.2 hardware? The slow speed and response times make it impossible to build projects for clients without complaints. The speed is unacceptable, and changing security settings or memory card doesn't help.
Switching back to web editor 1.0 brings much better speed than 1.1. However, version 1.0 lacks decimal points, trend graphs, and text formatting options.

Unfortunately, don't expect a quick solution. Since development moved abroad, everything slowed down—bug fixes and service packs are rare. I reported a web editor 1.1 bug in March 2021 and was told it would be forwarded. Nine months later, still no action; when development was in Germany, things were different.

Don't expect a quick solution. Since development moved to another country, bug fixes and updates have slowed. I reported an issue months ago and haven't seen changes. Strange how identical hardware performs so differently with web editor versions. I hope a firmware update or new editor version improves SD card read/write speeds soon.

As of August 2022, loading projects from the web editor to hardware is still extremely slow, sometimes taking 20 minutes. Opening web pages, especially for the first load, is painfully slow. The system could be great if not for these speed issues, making it unsuitable for professional use.

I suspect the SD card read/write is too slow because the web pages are stored there. If that's not the cause, maybe the web editor itself limits transfer speed. I hope performance can be improved soon.

The SD card type definitely affects transmission times. I tested with two types in the same 8.3 hardware and project: MicroSDHC Class 10 (16GB) took about 3 minutes, while an older San Disk Micro SD (2GB) took 6.5 minutes. Tests were done in a home network.

It's 2023 and the speed problems remain. I uploaded a blank website to both versions of hardware and measured load times after login: 8.2 takes ~10s, 8.3 about ~30s (HTTP version). Adding extra buttons and images only made 8.3 slower. Loading a larger multi-page project on 8.3 took 42s; it was much faster on 8.2. Tried using Amazon cloud as a workaround with 8.3, but it can't handle more complex content from newer web editor versions. My workaround: create the website with web editor 1.0.1, edit manually, and then upload to the hardware—still frustrating.

I'm seeing the same issue: since versions 1.1 and 1.1.1, websites are often inaccessible or at least five times slower using 8.3 hardware, even in non-secure mode. Developer tools in Chrome show problematic files and slow load times; these files are notably faster on 8.2 hardware with the same editor version. After contacting my distributor and the support service, they confirmed the issue. They will inform the product manager, since this affects the commercial promise of embedded websites.
You may have to wait a long time. There won't be a solution for 8.3 hardware. If anything, maybe a fix will come with future product versions.

This appears to be a case of inadequate firmware programming and a lack of interest in addressing bugs. The hardware shouldn't be so much slower than older versions. Moving development to China seems to have worsened things. Older product lines are already end-of-life, so customers are stuck with flawed 8.3 versions, and [company_name] doesn't seem to mind.
I just received the latest hardware (article_no hidden, version_no hidden) and the problem seems resolved. Speed is now much better.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report that newer hardware and web editor versions cause major slowdowns in project loading and web page performance. This occurs in both secure (HTTPS) and non-secure (HTTP) communication modes. Previous hardware and editor versions did not have such issues. Security changes are cited as the reason for the slowdown, but users believe the impact should be minimal and are frustrated by the lack of options to choose between secure and non-secure modes.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect communication and loading speeds with new hardware and software to match or only slightly lag behind previous versions. They want the ability to select desired levels of security for communication.
